tldr: The thread starts with hands-on, browser-based use of Claude's coding tools (a Jun 22 how-to on running Claude Code in the browser), then converges on a science-specific product. On Jun 30 Anthropic packaged that direction into Claude Science, a dedicated workbench for researchers.
whats_new: Anthropic launched Claude Science (Jun 30), a customizable AI workbench for scientists that integrates the tools and packages researchers most use, produces auditable artifacts, and offers flexible compute access — and a same-day Modal integration adds elastic, on-demand compute.
why_it_matters: Claude Science ships as a customizable app with auditable artifacts and pluggable compute, and the day-one Modal integration shows the workbench is open to external elastic-compute backends rather than a closed appliance. For engineers building research or agent tooling on Anthropic's stack, that's a platform to target rather than rebuild.

status.detail: Claude Science launched as an AI workbench for scientists, with a same-day third-party compute integration (Modal).

beats.headline: Claude Code goes browser-based
beats.summary: A how-to on running Claude Code directly in the browser — hands-on use of Claude's coding tools ahead of the science workbench.

beats.headline: Claude Science debuts as an AI workbench for scientists
beats.summary: A customizable app that integrates researchers' common tools and packages, produces auditable artifacts, and provides flexible access to computing resources.

beats.headline: Modal integration brings elastic compute to Claude Science
beats.summary: A same-day integration adds Modal's elastic compute for researchers on demand.

open_questions: Is Claude Science generally available, or limited/waitlisted? The launch note doesn't state access terms.
What format are the 'auditable artifacts', and are they exportable or interoperable with existing research tooling?
Will compute providers beyond Modal integrate, or is elastic compute effectively single-vendor for now?
Does the customizable app support self-hosted or arbitrary tools and packages, or a curated set?
take_for_builders: If you build research or agent tooling on Anthropic's stack, evaluate Claude Science as a target platform rather than rebuilding the workbench: check the auditable-artifact format for interoperability and confirm how the pluggable-compute model (Modal integration) maps to your infra before committing.
